clue.text: Mute foe thought man knew sod all. Rubbish! He has it all here!

indicators.note: calling the preceding words rubbish invites us to throw their letters about and rebuild them

explanation.surface: Someone scornfully dismisses a know-nothing enemy, then points to a place where every bit of wisdom is stored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish!' looks like an exclamation of contempt but signals that all twenty-seven letters of 'Mute foe thought man knew sod all' are to be rearranged. 'He has ... here!' frames the definition 'it all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Everything that people collectively know amounts to the whole lot, informally everything there is: 'it all'.

clue.text: 12 line in speech from Saki

indicators.note: in speech means the words are to be said out loud and heard as something else

parts.note: a cross-reference to the answer of 12 across, a word meaning mortal or personlike; a row is a line of things side by side

explanation.surface: A quotation from the Edwardian short-story writer Saki, numbered as line 12.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' stands for the answer at 12 across; said with ROW, it sounds like the writer's given names and surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Saki was the pen name of the writer Hector Hugh Munro, so the pseudonym defines the real name.

clue.text: Raspberries emitted by tinned French horn

annotationWithheld.why: Raspberries emitted by tinned French horn (5): SCORN is COR (French horn) in SN, but 'tinned' must give tin's symbol SN and also be the container indicator, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Raspberries emitted by tinned French horn

clue.text: Two thousands without insurance or capital

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the thousands surround the insurance

parts.note: M (Roman numeral) and K (kilo) both stand for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone is facing a two-thousand bill because they had no insurance or savings to fall back on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking' but means outside here; 'capital' looks like money but is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: Minsk is the capital city of Belarus.

clue.text: One correcting awful stoop injecting Ecstasy at hospital

indicators.note: injecting means taking another piece inside, so the jumbled stoop takes in the drug
awful suggests something badly made, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is slang for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: A medic treating a patient's terrible posture by giving them an illegal drug in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges STOOP to OSTOP; 'injecting' puts E inside it to give OSTEOP.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats the body by manipulating bones and muscles, so is one who corrects posture and joints.

clue.text: Confound circles when backing a horse

parts.note: to confound is to dismay or shock, to appal
O is a circle, so two of them for circles

indicators.note: backing means going in reverse, so the word for when is turned around

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: A punter is baffled at the racecourse, going round in circles while betting on a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like betting on a horse in the surface but turns AS into SA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Appaloosa is a North American breed of horse with a spotted coat.

clue.text: One knight died upright

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An honourable knight who died standing tall.
explanation.definitionFit: Something standing on its end is vertical, in other words upright.

clue.text: With which ramblers wildly caught sight of acres

indicators.note: wildly suggests disorder, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Walkers in the countryside suddenly spotting broad fields ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges C with SIGHT OF ACRES; the whole clue describes the legal entitlement walkers use to cross land.
explanation.definitionFit: A right of access is the legal permission that lets walkers cross private land, so ramblers go with it.

clue.text: She engages with our poor planet's pollutant

indicators.note: poor suggests something in bad shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A campaigner worries about the harm being done to our poor Earth by pollution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link joining the two fodder groups; 'poor' looks like sympathy for the planet but rearranges SHE ENGAGES OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbon dioxide and methane are examples of gases that trap heat and pollute the Earth's atmosphere.

clue.text: Nail so digitally invasive

parts.note: a toenail that pushes into the flesh of the toe, a digit, has grown inward

explanation.surface: A nail that intrudes into a finger or toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'digitally' pretends to be about computers but refers to digits, fingers and toes.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail whose edge has grown into the surrounding skin is the classic example of this painful condition.

clue.text: It's selected for Jeremy Clarkson's vehicle

definitions.meaning: the highest gear, chosen by a driver for cruising at speed
the BBC motoring programme that made Jeremy Clarkson a star, a vehicle in the sense of a showcase

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the highest gear of a car and the name of the TV show Clarkson presented.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
Had one with interfering daughter

indicators.note: interfering means getting in between, so one letter is placed inside the word for one

explanation.surface: A parent had one child, with a meddling daughter getting involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link word but gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: To have owned something is to have had it in your possession.

clue.text: Dispatch deer protecting fox at entry of hounds

indicators.note: protecting means wrapping round, so the deer encloses the fox

parts.note: a doe is a female deer
tod is an old and dialect word for a fox

indicators.note: entry of means the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A hunting scene: a deer shelters a fox as the hounds come in.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD is a dialect word for a fox, worth remembering for crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispatch something is to kill it, as is to do it to death.

clue.text: Bikini, say, worn by nanny? On the contrary, this Shiah wouldn't wear that!

indicators.note: something worn by someone goes around them, so the nanny encloses the atoll

parts.note: an ayah is a nanny or nursemaid in India
Bikini is an atoll in the Pacific, so an example of an atoll

explanation.surface: A joke picturing a nanny in a bikini, then noting that a Shia cleric would never wear one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bikini' is not swimwear but the Pacific atoll; 'On the contrary' and the rest are surface play telling us the cleric would not wear a bikini.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior religious leader among Shiite Muslims.

clue.text: Child left in a lift, he thought

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the child and left go inside the lift

parts.note: to rise is to lift up
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A child left behind in a lift, and someone reflecting on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' looks like an elevator but is the verb RISE; 'he thought' reads as reported musing but defines a philosopher.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the great Greek philosopher, a man whose work was thought itself.

clue.text: Dudley's superior mousetrap?

definitions.meaning: Robert Dudley was Earl of a county town, a title superior to his name
mousetrap is slang for cheap cheese that would bait a trap, here a red English cheese

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both Robert Dudley's earldom under Elizabeth I and a hard red English cheese.

clue.text: Dryden's imagination resembled the wings of what, Macaulay? Wild cat, one with horns

definitions.text: Dryden's imagination resembled the wings of what, Macaulay?

indicators.note: wild suggests something out of control, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A quotation question about the critic Macaulay on Dryden, followed by a strange horned wildcat.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay wrote that Dryden's imagination resembled the wings of a big flightless bird, helping it run but not fly. 'Wild' rearranges CAT, I and HORNS.
explanation.definitionFit: Macaulay's essay on Dryden compares his imagination to the wings of a flightless bird, useful for running but unable to soar.

clue.text: Now that is superior, the last word!

parts.note: AD, Anno Domini, marks the present era, so it can stand for now
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
U stands for upper class, superior

explanation.surface: Someone declaring triumphantly that they have had the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: A farewell is the last thing said on parting, so it is the last word.

clue.text: About sadly to update the French Revolution

parts.note: C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A historian sadly having to revise an account of the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges TO UPDATE; 'the French Revolution' looks like the historical event but means an overthrow named in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'etat is a sudden seizure of government, a revolution in a phrase borrowed from French.

clue.text: Computer inquiry throwing out child minders

indicators.note: the run of words throws out, or gives off, a word lying within them

explanation.surface: A computer query that ejects a child carer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'child minders' looks like babysitters but means wombs, which look after an unborn child.
explanation.definitionFit: Wombs shelter and nourish unborn children, so they are cheekily called child minders.

clue.text: Lamp runs central to Tubby Clayton's body

indicators.note: central to means placed in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: Toc H is the Christian movement founded by the Reverend Tubby Clayton
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A lamp held at the heart of a stout man's body.
explanation.walkthrough: Toc H, the soldiers' fellowship founded by Tubby Clayton in the First World War, has a lamp as its emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: A torch is a portable lamp, especially a battery-powered one.

clue.text: Name two setters without an original muse

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one setter surrounds the name

parts.note: a setter refers to themself as me, so two setters give that word twice
the second of the two setters, again me

explanation.surface: A request to name two crossword compilers who have no creative spark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking' but means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mneme, goddess of memory, was one of the three original Muses before the canonical nine.

clue.text: Parrot with bill stuck in gullet

indicators.note: stuck in means lodged inside the other piece

parts.note: a maw is the throat or gullet
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A parrot with something caught in its throat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a beak but means an account.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaw is a large brightly coloured parrot of Central and South America.

clue.text: Rod, one way to divine water

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: to divine is to work out by guessing, so the letters must be puzzled into a new order

explanation.surface: A dowsing rod is one way to find water underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is dowsing with a rod, but 'Rod, one' means a man called Rod, the rock singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Stewart is the British rock singer, one example of a Rod.

clue.text: Take one firm, dry active cheese

parts.note: R, from Latin recipe, means take on a prescription
I is the Roman numeral one
Co is short for company, a firm
TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry
A is short for active, in grammar

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: take one firm, dry, lively cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian cheese made from whey.

clue.text: Politician who had miracle recovery

indicators.note: recovery suggests putting something back together, so the letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A politician who made a miraculous comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Howard was a Conservative Home Secretary and party leader; 'recovery' rearranges WHO HAD MIRACLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Howard was a British Conservative politician who led his party from 2003 to 2005.
